key_insight: Safeguarded online learning can improve nonlinear conjugate gradient robustness while preserving its classical two-term, low-storage structure.
engineering_relevance: The approach is promising for PDE-constrained optimization where function and gradient evaluations are expensive.
method: Use two independent online extreme learning machines to predict recovery coefficients and bounded step-size corrections.
Accept predictions only when deterministic descent, scale, and out-of-distribution safeguards pass; otherwise retain deterministic recovery.
Train on existing optimization-trajectory data without additional function or gradient evaluations.
evidence_signal: Across 480 CUTEst problems, all six learning-assisted variants improved robustness at broadly comparable evaluation costs; a conductivity-identification example also illustrated potential cost and runtime reductions.
watch_item: Benefits may depend on safeguard and prediction-trigger settings, and the abstract does not establish performance guarantees beyond the tested problems.
paper_title: Safeguarded Learning-Assisted Nonlinear Conjugate Gradient Methods
